title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Amina Patel
description: Motivation: Improve Dedicated fleet autoscaler behavior for multi-priority routing and provide better burst token smoothing plus additional utilization reporting so SREs and customers can reason about capacity and burst costs. This PR implements: 1) priority-aware routing for the dedicated autoscaler so high-priority routes are favored under constrained capacity, 2) token-bucket smoothing and refill-rate tuning to reduce short-lived spike-induced scale-ups, 3) new per-fleet and per-priority utilization metrics (+Prometheus exposition) and dashboarding hooks, and 4) small UX / config additions to the Dedicated config schema and console. Scope: changes touch the autoscaler core, metrics plumbing, docs and tests. Checklist: - [x] Add priority routing policy and unit tests - [x] Implement token-bucket smoothing with configurable smoothing_factor - [x] Add dedicated_fleet_utilization_percent and autoscaler_burst_tokens metrics - [x] Update Dedicated config schema & validation - [x] Add integration test for burst smoothing under synthetic spike - [x] Update docs and release notes Related Linear: ENG-4321 (priority routing design), ENG-4390 (utilization reporting). Related Jira: SUP-1023 (customer-reported burst scale-ups). Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/priority-routing-design, docsite PR: redwood-docs#1421. Summary of approach: - Priority routing: introduce a two-tier allocation loop in services/autoscaler/allocator.go that first satisfies high-priority routes by estimating available tokens per pool and reserving a headroom margin, then allocates remaining capacity to lower priorities. The algorithm uses existing score heuristics but adds "priority_multiplier" per route that is configurable. - Token-bucket smoothing: implement a refill-based smoothing layer in services/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go. Instead of immediate token replenishment on instance add, we apply an exponential smoothing factor (smoothing_factor, default 0.25) to the token refill path and persist refill state to the autoscaler store to avoid oscillation on quick spikes. - Utilization reporting: expose dedicated_fleet_utilization_percent and dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens with labels (fleet_id, region, priority). Also emit derived metrics per-route for console dashboards. - Backwards compatibility: config additions are optional; default behavior unchanged. Migration: no data migrations required; metric names are additive. Testing notes: Unit tests for allocator and tokenbucket added under services/autoscaler/*. Integration test simulates a 30s spike and asserts no more than 1 unneeded scale-up per spike. CI showed an initial flaky integration test due to a token refill race that was fixed in commit "fix/token-refill-race". Merge: squash and merge after approvals.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice work. Two high-level asks: 1) ensure any new metric cardinality is bounded (we should avoid unbounded route labels) and 2) add a feature flag for smoothing so we can roll it out. Please add explanations in the allocator docs.

Amina Patel: Responding: added a cardinality cap by limiting route label to top-50 hot routes and added 'enable_burst_smoothing' feature flag (false by default). Updated docs to describe rollout plan.

Jing Wei: Integration test flaky on first run, failing on race in token refill. Suggest adding a small lock around refill state updates or using compare-and-swap. Also add a deterministic clock to the integration test.
Amina Patel: Fixed in commit 'fix/token-refill-race' — switched to CAS on the refill state and injected deterministic clock into integration test. Reran CI locally and in pipeline.
Samir Khan (approval): Tests look good and instrumentation is helpful for SRE. Approving — please squash and merge once CI is green.

release_notes:
- Improve dedicated autoscaler: priority-aware routing to protect high-priority routes under constrained capacity.
- Reduce noisy scale-ups: optional burst token-bucket smoothing with configurable smoothing_factor and enable_burst_smoothing flag.
- Added utilization metrics: dedicated_fleet_utilization_percent and dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens (labels: fleet_id, region, priority).
- Backwards compatible; default behavior unchanged.
